obligations.scenario: Starting from reset, compute the padded abc block, all-0, all-1, distinct-word, and random blocks in sequence. For both modes, use an independent 64-round whole-block mathematical algorithm to compute the full 256-bit result; also check the standard SHA-256 and the first 224 bits of SHA-224 for abc.
obligations.checked_target: All operations use 32-bit unsigned arithmetic modulo 2^32. Each 512-bit input block is divided into W[0..15], most significant word first. For t=16..63, W[t]=W[t-16]+σ0(W[t-15])+W[t-7]+σ1(W[t-2]), where σ0(x)=ROTR7(x) XOR ROTR18(x) XOR SHR3(x) and σ1(x)=ROTR17(x) XOR ROTR19(x) XOR SHR10(x). Initialize a..h from the current eight-word chaining value; in each of 64 rounds, use T1=h+Σ1(e)+Ch(e,f,g)+K[t]+W[t] and T2=Σ0(a)+Maj(a,b,c), and update (a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h)=(T1+T2,a,b,c,d+T1,e,f,g). Σ0 is ROTR2 XOR ROTR13 XOR ROTR22, Σ1 is ROTR6 XOR ROTR11 XOR ROTR25, Ch=(e AND f) XOR ((NOT e) AND g), and Maj=(a AND b) XOR (a AND c) XOR (b AND c). K[t] consists of the 64 constants from the SHA-256 standard, namely the fractional parts of the cube roots of the first 64 primes multiplied by 2^32 and rounded down. The result is the eight input chaining words respectively added to a..h after 64 rounds, with H0 occupying the most significant 32 bits. The initial eight words for SHA-256 are 6a09e667 bb67ae85 3c6ef372 a54ff53a 510e527f 9b05688c 1f83d9ab 5be0cd19; the initial eight words for SHA-224 are c1059ed8 367cd507 3070dd17 f70e5939 ffc00b31 68581511 64f98fa7 befa4fa4. The full 256-bit chaining value is output here, and SHA-224 also retains the eighth word; the module does not generate padding, length encoding, or external byte-order conversion.

A next directly after reset starts from an all-0 chaining value.

obligations.scenario: For a single block and a continuation block, sample every cycle from n through n+67, then remain idle for 80 cycles and check that the digest and valid hold. Check that it is still busy at n+64 and completes at n+65.
obligations.checked_target: The 65th rising edge after acceptance edge n (n+65) updates digest to the final compression value, with ready=1 and digest_valid=1 at the same time. It remains busy from n+1 through n+64, without early completion; during computation, digest retains the chaining value at acceptance. digest_valid remains 1 until the next valid command or reset; digest is retained while idle.

reset.definition: First produce a nonzero digest and start another block
Assert reset_n between adjacent clk edges and observe between edges
Remain idle after releasing reset and restart

launch.definition: Apply init, next, and both asserted simultaneously in separate cases
Change the entire 512-bit block after acceptance to verify capture

algorithm.definition: Apply abc, all zeros, all ones, blocks with every word different, and random blocks in each of the two modes
Compare all 256 bits using an independent full-block 64-round algorithm, and compare against the standard abc results

chain.definition: At least three distinct next blocks after init, with mode changes
Directly issue next after reset and compute from the all-zero chaining value

retire.definition: Observe cycle by cycle from n through n+67 and distinguish n+64 from n+65
Remain idle for at least 80 cycles after completion and check that digest and valid are retained

busy.definition: Perturb the commands and block at rising edges 1, 10, 64, and 65 after acceptance
Compare the first block's result and verify that no queuing occurs
Hold the command across the completion edge and check for restart at the next idle edge

held.definition: Hold init and next continuously in separate cases across at least two completions
Change block and check acceptance of all 512 bits on every idle acceptance
Include both modes and the full 256-bit digest in the checks
